steps.notes: Literal-header impl (linspace(log(min_price),log(max_price))) PASSES, but only because tests swap min/max positionally; frozen target is a DESCENDING grid with negative dp. Contract-respecting (normalized) variant FAILS; docstring-literal (N,1) column-shape variant FAILS.

Index-literal impl with CALL payoff at V[:,-1], V[0,:]=0, V[-1,:]=exp(p[-1])-K*exp(-r(1-T)) PASSES. Literal background formula max(K-s,0) FAILS; physically-faithful by-value boundary placement FAILS; reversed corner application order FAILS.

scipy.sparse tridiag(a,b,c) on (sub,diag,super) PASSES; a,b,c match background formulas exactly. Dense ndarray return CRASHES on test's .toarray(). Background recurrence has typo (c multiplies V^n_{j-1} instead of V^n_{j+1}).

Backward march from terminal column: V^n_inner = spsolve(D, V^{n+1}_inner - B^n), B^n=(a*V[0,n],0..0,c*V[-1,n]) PASSES. Test inputs are out-of-contract (descending p, dp<0) via the same swapped initialize_grid call. Docstring claims D shape (N_t-2)x(N_t-2); actual is (N_p-2)x(N_p-2).

Composition per literal headers PASSES (~15 s for all 3 tests). Note: 63.5 targets are on an ASCENDING grid (gold called initialize_grid in header order internally), while 63.1/63.2/63.4 targets are on the descending grid from the swapped test calls — only order-agnostic index-literal implementations satisfy both regimes.

PASSES only with linear interpolation across the price grid at time column int(t*time_step). Nearest-grid-point lookup FAILS (rel err ~1e-3 >> rtol 1e-5); adjacent time column 1499 FAILS. Test 0 queries S0=100 below the grid's min price 200 (target 0.0 = clamp artifact).

findings.evidence: Header: `def initialize_grid(price_step, time_step, strike, max_price, min_price)`. ALL tests of 63.1 (and the test code of 63.2 and 63.4) call `initialize_grid(price_step,time_step,strike, min_price, max_price)` — e.g. 63.1 test 0 sets `min_price = 20 / max_price = 500` and passes them in that order, so inside the function max_price=20 and min_price=500, inverting the documented semantics ('max_price: ...set a max bound', 'min_price: avoiding 0 as a bound'). The frozen h5 target encodes the result of running the literal code on these swapped inputs: p = [6.2146... -> 2.9957...] i.e. linspace(log(500), log(20), 5000), DESCENDING, with dp = -6.439e-4 (negative). Probe: a contract-respecting implementation that normalizes `lo,hi = min(...),max(...)` FAILS steptest 63.1 (verified, review/work/63/variant_sorted_grid.py); the blind-literal implementation PASSES. Matches v3 pattern 'out-of-contract test inputs'.
findings.suggested_fix: Swap the last two arguments in the test-case calls of steps 63.1, 63.2 and 63.4 to `initialize_grid(price_step, time_step, strike, max_price, min_price)` and regenerate the h5 targets for 63.1, 63.2 and 63.4 (63.5/63.6 targets are already on the ascending grid and stay valid). Alternatively rename the header params to match the calls — but then 63.5/63.6 gold behavior (ascending grid) must be regenerated instead.

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'p: ... shape: price_step * 1' and 'T: ... shape: time_step * 1'; step 63.2's docstring instead says 'p: ... (shape = 1 * N_p)'. The frozen targets are plain 1-D arrays of shape (price_step,)/(time_step,). A solver literally returning the documented column shape (N,1) FAILS: cmp_tuple_or_list uses np.allclose, which broadcasts (5000,1) against (5000,) to (5000,5000) and returns False (verified FAIL, review/work/63/variant_column_shape.py).
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstrings to 'shape: (price_step,)' / 'shape: (time_step,)' and make 63.2's description consistent.

findings.evidence: The step background states the temporal boundary condition as '$V(t_{max},p) = max(K-s,0)$' — that is the PUT payoff. The frozen target encodes the CALL payoff max(s-K,0): test 0 target V[1,-1] = 1494.6997 = exp(p[1]) - 1000 (s-K), where the stated formula would give 0. The surrounding prose ('buy at the strike price and sell the stocks at market price', 'European call option' in docstring, main description 'Use appropriate boundary condition for call options') implies the call payoff, but the only explicit equation given contradicts it. Probe: implementing the stated formula max(K-s,0) FAILS steptest 63.2 (verified, review/work/63/variant_put_payoff.py).
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the background equation to V(t_max, p) = max(s - K, 0).

findings.evidence: Because 63.2's test code feeds the swapped (descending) grid from 63.1, the frozen target places the 's -> 0 => V = 0' boundary at the HIGHEST-price row (target V[0,:]=0 with exp(p[0])=2500) and the p_max formula s_max - K*exp(-r(T-t)) at the LOWEST-price row, yielding negative European-call prices: target V[-1,:] runs from -680.199 (=300 - 1000*e^{-0.02}) to -700.0. Only implementations that assign boundaries blindly by index (row 0 = 'p_min side', row -1 = 'p_max side', s_max := exp(p[-1])) reproduce this. A physically-faithful implementation that places boundaries at the actual min/max price rows (e.g. via argmin/argmax of exp(p), or s_max := exp(p).max()) — exactly what the background prose describes ('if stock price go to zero...', 'if price rises by a lot (here, p = p_max)') — FAILS steptest 63.2 (verified, review/work/63/variant_value_bc.py).
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the swapped initialize_grid call in 63.2's test code (see 63.1 finding) and regenerate targets so the grid is ascending and the boundary values are physically meaningful (no negative call prices).

findings.evidence: At the two corner cells the price boundary must OVERWRITE the terminal payoff: target V[0,-1]=0 (payoff would be 1500) and V[-1,-1]=-700 (payoff would be 0). The background only hints at this ('Consider temporal boundary condition first.'). Probe: applying price boundaries first and payoff last differs in exactly those 2 cells and FAILS np.allclose over the whole array (verified, review/work/63/variant_corner_order.py).
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly in the docstring that the payoff is written first and the price boundary rows take precedence at the corners (or compare only interior+edges separately).

findings.evidence: Docstring return spec says only 'D: The tri-diagonal matrix constructed for the finite difference method' — no return type stated. Every test calls `construct_matrix(...).toarray()`, which requires a scipy.sparse object. A numerically correct dense ndarray implementation crashes: "AttributeError: 'numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'toarray'" (verified FAIL, review/work/63/variant_dense_matrix.py). Mitigation: required_dependencies import `from scipy import sparse` and `spsolve`, which hints at sparse, hence confidence medium on real-world score impact.
findings.suggested_fix: State 'returns a scipy.sparse matrix' in the docstring, or make the test tolerant: `D = construct_matrix(...); D = D.toarray() if hasattr(D, 'toarray') else D`.

findings.evidence: Background recurrence is written '$V^{n+1}_j=aV^n_{j-1}+bV^n_j+cV^n_{j-1}$' — V^n_{j-1} appears twice; the last term should be cV^n_{j+1}. Resolvable from the full discretized equation directly above it and from the a,b,c definitions (targets confirm a on the sub-diagonal, c on the super-diagonal).
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the typo: V^{n+1}_j = a V^n_{j-1} + b V^n_j + c V^n_{j+1}.

findings.evidence: 63.4's own test code repeats the swapped call `initialize_grid(N_p,N_t,strike, min_price, max_price)`, so V (from 63.2) and dp (negative, -3.222e-3 in test 0) are out-of-contract relative to the documented grid semantics. The target was generated on this inverted grid: target V[-1,0] = -375.615 = 100 - 500*e^{-0.05} (a negative 'call price' at the lowest-price row). Any solver whose initialize_grid/apply_boundary_conditions deviates from blind index-literalism (the failing-but-reasonable variants documented under 63.1/63.2) is re-penalized here; an implementation assuming dp>0 (e.g. using |dp| or rebuilding the grid ascending) also fails. The forward_iteration logic itself is sign-agnostic, so conditional on literal steps 1-3 the step passes (verified PASS with B^n at time n: V^n = spsolve(D, V^{n+1} - B^n)).
findings.suggested_fix: Same root fix as 63.1: correct the argument order in 63.4's test code and regenerate the 63.4 targets on the ascending grid.

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'D: The tri-diagonal matrix ... Shape: (N_t-2) x (N_t-2)'. Actual D (from 63.3, confirmed by its targets) is (N_p-2) x (N_p-2); tests use N_p=1000 vs N_t=2000 so the claim is materially wrong. A solver sizing the boundary vector B as N_t-2 from this docstring would crash.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the docstring to Shape: (N_p-2) x (N_p-2).

findings.evidence: Prompt/docstring say only 'Outputs: Price of the option at time t * time_step' — nothing about how to read the price off the grid. The target requires LINEAR INTERPOLATION across the price grid at time column int(t*time_step): np.interp(log(S0), p, V[:,1500]) = 43.85910767718888 vs target 43.85910767618714 (rel 2.3e-11; interp in s-space also passes at rel 3.8e-7). The equally natural nearest-grid-point lookup gives 43.90364 (rel err 1.0e-3 >> rtol 1e-5) and FAILS steptest officially (verified); floor-index gives 43.75495 (fails); using time column 1499 (e.g. argmin|T-t| tie or int(t*(N_t-1))) gives 43.90005 (rel 1.0e-3, fails). The lookup convention is decisive and unstated.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the docstring: 'interpolate linearly between the two neighboring price grid points at time index int(t * time_step)'.

findings.evidence: Test 0 queries S0=100 with strike=1000 and min_price=(1/5)*strike=200, i.e. the queried stock price lies BELOW the documented lower bound of the price grid [200, 5000]. Target is exactly 0.0, which matches np.interp's silent clamping to the V=0 lower boundary (and nearest-index lookup). An implementation that extrapolates (scipy interp1d fill_value='extrapolate') or validates the domain fails/raises. Note the true Black-Scholes value at S0=100 (sig=1, tau=1, r=0.05) is ~1.17, so 0.0 is purely a truncated-domain/clamp artifact.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose S0 within [min_price, max_price] in test 0, or document the required clamping behavior for out-of-range S0.

overall_assessment: All 6 steps are solvable and pass under a single fully index-literal implementation (verified end-to-end with steptest, joint mode), so the problem is not broken outright. However, it is booby-trapped: the tests of 63.1/63.2/63.4 call initialize_grid with min/max swapped relative to the header, so their frozen targets live on a descending log-price grid with negative dp and physically impossible boundary values (negative call prices), while 63.5/63.6 targets live on the correct ascending grid; any solver who validates inputs, normalizes the grid, or honors the physics prose is mis-scored on up to 3 steps. Additional independent traps: the only explicit payoff equation in 63.2's background is the put payoff (target encodes call), 63.3's test demands a scipy.sparse return that the spec never states, and 63.6 requires an unstated linear-interpolation read-off (nearest-grid-point fails by 1e-3 relative). Recommend fixing the argument order + regenerating targets for 63.1/63.2/63.4, correcting the payoff formula, and pinning the sparse return type and interpolation convention.
